sources.title: ABLIC S-1200, Rev.6 p10: input/output capacitance and ESR
sources.finding: Candidate U1 permits input and output capacitance >=0.1 uF; output ESR <=1 ohm. This is a design constraint, not the PetSafe BOM.

sources.title: ABLIC S-812C, Rev.7 p18: output capacitor purpose
sources.finding: Candidate U6 can be stable without an output capacitor; the capacitor improves transient response. It does not force C37 to a particular value.

sources.title: SGMICRO SGM8542, pp9-10: bypassing and low-pass feedback
sources.finding: The example supply network uses 10 uF plus 0.1 uF (or 0.01 uF). The inverting feedback example gives gain -Rf/Rin and a pole 1/(2*pi*Rf*C). No exact PetSafe receiver reference schematic is established.

sources.title: Microchip 8-bit PIC design recommendations
sources.finding: Recommends 100 nF local VDD/VSS bypassing. Warns that MCLR capacitance can affect programming; do not blindly assign C35 as a generic debounce capacitor.

sources.title: TI SN74LVC2G14 candidate datasheet
sources.finding: Reference for candidate U2 input thresholds and supply limits; candidate identity remains unresolved at the measured 6.3-V supply. No assumed threshold used to finalize C8/C9.

sources.title: Microchip AN710: Antenna Circuit Design
sources.finding: Resonant antenna design depends on inductance and the equivalent capacitance/loading, not frequency alone.

sources.title: PetSafe Microchip Cat Flap, PPA19-16811 SKU, FDX-B FAQ
sources.finding: Manufacturer page selected for the PPA19-16811 variant lists FDX-B compatibility and states 134.2 kHz. Supports that design target; actual PCB carrier has not been scoped.

sources.title: Murata capacitor selection guide
sources.finding: Capacitance, dielectric, voltage and size are separate selection parameters. Package dimensions alone do not recover the capacitance.

sources.title: Murata: capacitance under DC bias
sources.finding: High-permittivity ceramics can lose effective capacitance under DC bias; qualify effective capacitance at the operating rail when selecting replacements.

sources.title: Microchip AN710 in microID design guide, printed pp113-116
sources.finding: Series-resonant coil voltage can be Q times the sinusoidal drive voltage. Used for general LC theory only, not its 13.56-MHz component values or a PetSafe voltage prediction.

sources.title: TI SWRA284, Low-Frequency RFID in a Nutshell, pp7-10
sources.finding: LF example uses low-loss C0G/NP0 resonance capacitors and a switched trimming array to bring resonance to 134.2 kHz. Transponder example, not this reader schematic; no component values are transferred.

principles: All 44 unknown fitted ceramics now have numerical choices, proposed dielectric/rating and a stated basis. This is a complete candidate table, not a factory BOM.
All 44 candidates are displayed in native v0.9.44 with an asterisk. Copper connections, measured values and population status are unchanged. Original-value uncertainty remains explicit.
The 12 supply choices are conventional replacement candidates; 17 signal/timing choices require circuit validation; 15 antenna entries form one deliberate design example.
Reference circuits constrain functions and sensible ranges; no evidence establishes that PetSafe copied an exact reference design.
Antenna inductance is now user-reported as 500 uH with test conditions unspecified. RF voltage, individual capacitor values and branch weights/order remain unverified.
All components remain fitted. Scope work remains deferred. No new broad multimeter or LCR campaign is requested.

calculations.resonance_frequency_status: 134.2-kHz design target supported by manufacturer product-variant FAQ; actual PCB waveform not measured.
calculations.caveat: Simple LC examples bound an equivalent total, not the fifteen physical capacitor values. Winding resistance near 5 ohm cannot determine inductance.

next_actions: Use the complete candidate table for analysis and comparison. Preserve C5 and all six DNP options exactly as established.

For the next RF validation phase, qualify the reported antenna inductance/equivalent resonance and observe carrier, capacitor peak voltage and actual switch action. That qualifies the bank as a whole instead of guessing 15 independent values.
Then check receiver bandwidth/settling and Q8 gate overlap with the chosen timing candidates; candidate IC identities and firmware assumptions still matter.
Ordinary bypass values can be qualified in groups by effective capacitance, stability and transient response; no need to request 44 isolated-value measurements now.

antenna_design_example.inductance_status: Owner now reports measured 500 uH. Frequency, instrument, isolation and Q were not specified; earlier seed used this as an assumption.
assumptions: Each transistor is approximated only as an ideal open/closed link from its switched capacitor to ground. The disputed PNP candidate does not establish this AC behavior.
All five series/parallel branches act in parallel from ANT2 to ground. The coil runs from driven ANT1 to ANT2.
Ignore switch capacitance, coil self-capacitance, detector loading, losses and harmonic/nonlinear operation.
Ascending branch weights assigned to Q3/Q4/Q5/Q6/Q11 are arbitrary; existing PIC firmware may expect a different order or algorithm.
antenna_design_example.scaling: With the reported 500 uH the 134.2-kHz target requires about 2.813 nF. If a later qualified antenna measurement differs, scale the candidate bank by 500 uH / actual inductance, then account for parasitics and losses.
antenna_design_example.why_five: Five independent controls permit up to 32 switch states. Near-binary effective increments make fine tuning plausible. Actual distinct resonances, binary weights and automatic tuning are not established.
antenna_design_example.alternate_explanations: A thermometer-coded or mixed coarse/fine bank is also possible. A fixed carrier does not require five different chip frequencies.

voltage_review.supply: 6.3 V is measured operating voltage, not a capacitor voltage rating. For ordinary rail capacitors choose 16 V on 3.3/4.5-V rails and 25 V on 6.3-V rails as starting ratings; existing C5 is known 16 V.
voltage_review.resonance: A simple series LC at resonance has |Vc| approximately Q times the sinusoidal drive component. A 0-to-6.3-V 50%-duty square wave has a 4.01-V-peak fundamental. Illustrative loaded Q=10 or 20 gives about 40 or 80 V peak across the equivalent resonant reactance. These are examples, not this PCB measurements; individual capacitors share voltage according to their branch.
voltage_review.bank_selection: Select 250-V C0G/NP0, 5% as a conservative design seed for all 15 tank parts. This is not an inferred original rating or a certified safe maximum; later peak/RMS voltage, AC loss, switch stress and package-fit checks may justify another choice.
voltage_review.detector_selection: C19/C20 get a provisional 100-V rating because their node is coupled to ANT2 through D2; actual clamping behavior and peak stress remain unverified.
voltage_review.size: Within a known dielectric and voltage family, larger size often permits greater capacitance. Across different circuit roles, a larger low-loss/high-voltage RF part can have less capacitance than a small supply bypass. Size is supporting evidence, not a value code.
